story_pergunta: At your company, who checks whether AI engines cite your content?

slides.eyebrow: AI ON THE RISE · GOOGLE AI MODE
slides.headline: AI Mode answers harder questions. Does it cite you?
slides.sub: A smarter Search changes who gets seen, and who gets left out.

slides.headline: Google upgraded Search with Gemini 4, aimed at complex questions
slides.body: Per TechCrunch, Google calls it its biggest model improvement to Search yet. Multi-part questions, very specific requests and even typos should be handled better, with more visual answers and a wider range of links.

slides.headline: What the upgrade changes for your content
items: Search breaks one question into several subqueries (query fan-out)
Answers include comparison tables, images and structured responses
Google says users will be connected to sites they might have missed

slides.headline: What I see in companies: nobody knows if AI cites them
items: Content is written for people, not for machines that retrieve and quote it
Teams track rankings and clicks, but not AI crawling or citations
Nobody owns the question: is our brand being read by AI engines?

slides.headline: One of Brazil's largest cosmetics companies already has this
items: Annual report rebuilt: 3-language server-rendered HTML, JSON-LD, llms.txt, 17 AI crawlers allowed
1,427 reads by AI crawlers from 8 engines, plus 553 searches from a real person's question
60 people reached the site by clicking an AI citation, in 15 days of measurement

slides.headline: Measure instead of assuming.
slides.body: A smarter AI Mode makes citation more valuable, but it doesn't tell you whether you're getting it. In my work, an in-house log collector separates crawling, real questions and citation clicks. Without that split, you are guessing.

slides.eyebrow: WANT TO SEE HOW I DID IT?
slides.headline: Comment GEO.
slides.body: I'll send you the step-by-step of this case by DM. I take AI off the drawing board and put it into production, with measured results.

caption:
Google upgraded Search with Gemini 4, and TechCrunch reports it calls this its biggest model improvement to Search yet. The pitch: better handling of multi-part questions, very specific requests and typos, plus more visual answers and a broader range of links through query fan-out.

In practice, this suggests the question is no longer only "do we rank?" It is "can an AI system retrieve our content, understand it and cite it?"

What I see in companies: content is written for people only, and nobody measures what AI engines do with it. Teams watch rankings and clicks. Few watch crawling, real questions or citation clicks.

I worked on this with one of Brazil's largest cosmetics companies. We rebuilt an annual report to be read and cited by ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity: server-rendered HTML in 3 languages, Schema.org/JSON-LD, llms.txt and 17 AI crawlers allowed by name. In 15 days of measurement: 1,427 reads by AI crawlers from 8 engines, 553 searches triggered by a real person asking a question, and 60 people who arrived by clicking an AI citation.

Measure instead of assuming.

Comment GEO and I'll DM you how I did it.

Sources: blog.google, techcrunch.com
